user-stories.text: A terminal is a lightweight Web2 application with cryptographic capabilities. Its purpose and risk policy guide chainpoint selection, anchor acceptance and asset verification. The user can then build a transaction or consume verified data off-chain. The role diagram shows anchors providing roots, untrusted ledger providers serving data and proofs, application services constructing proofs and terminals verifying before use.

choose-trust-and-buy-availability.text: Running your own anchor is the optimal deal for trust independence. Chosen institutional publications are an exceptionally attractive operational deal under explicit institutional trust. Both let applications buy capacity. Follow the trust and availability page for the assumptions.

read-the-design.text: Start with runnable root acceptance and selected point session journeys. Inspect trusted and untrusted publications, exact session acquisition, absence and newer point refusal. Continue through concepts, trust choices, architecture, chainpoint sessions, evidence and the roadmap.

repository-scope.text: Lockness owns cross-project design and acceptance. Component repositories own implementation. CSMT-UTXO supplies commitment machinery; the ledger provider still needs substantial storage and query work.

check-the-documentation.text: The model gate checks pinned Lean proofs, axiom dependencies, production semantic counterexamples, root and session scenarios, repeated reads and expiry refusal. Session acquisition preserves arbitrary provider offers at the exact point; it does not prove root trust. The documentation gate checks diagram and speech freshness and builds the site. Just CI runs both. Model properties do not establish component implementation or deployment.
